item.title: Chimagen's myeloma trispecific — GSK buys a preclinical T cell engager and won't name its two tumor targets
item.description: Posted 2026-09-15: GSK announced (07:03 ET) it has entered an agreement to acquire a PRECLINICAL trispecific T cell engager for multiple myeloma from Chimagen Biosciences. Terms: full global rights, UNDISCLOSED upfront, success-based development and commercial milestones to a total potential value of up to $750M. Phase 1 expected 2027. GSK describes the asset only as binding T cells plus "two strategically selected and validated tumour-associated antigens" - THE TARGETS ARE NOT DISCLOSED, in contrast to the 2024 deal which named CD19 and CD20 in the headline. DEAL CONTEXT: this is GSK's SECOND Chimagen acquisition. October 2024: $300M upfront plus $550M milestones ($850M total) for CMG1A46, a clinical-stage CD19 x CD20 x CD3 engager now in Phase 1 for B-cell malignancies and B-cell-dependent autoimmune disease (SLE, lupus nephritis). Today's headline total is SMALLER and the upfront undisclosed, for an asset that has never been in a human - read the undisclosed upfront the way undisclosed upfronts are normally read. THE PLATFORM IS THE ASSET: Chimagen's TRIAD platform builds an IgG-like ~151 kDa trispecific in "1:(1+1)" valency - ONE deliberately LOW-AFFINITY CD3 arm plus one high-affinity arm each against two tumor antigens. Selectivity from avidity, not affinity. CMG1A46 preclinical package (ASH 2020): PBMC-mediated tumor lysis EC50 ~0.3 pM; cynomolgus monkeys tolerated 3 mg/kg vs 0.5 mg/kg for a conventional CD3 x CD20 bispecific (6x) with no noticeable increase in toxicity, and up to 10 mg/kg without significant AEs; CD3 receptor occupancy transiently spiked then SUSTAINED at only 20-30%; cytokines peaked 4-8h after first dose and returned to baseline within 24h; serum half-life >70h. THE DISAGREEMENT WITH GSK'S RATIONALE: the release leads on tolerability ("TCEs have been associated with difficult tolerability profiles"). That claim is roughly a year out of date. J and J's JNJ-79635322 (JNJ-5322), a BCMA x GPRC5D x CD3 trispecific, reported first-in-human Phase 1 at ASCO 2025 (NCT05652335): 126 patients, 8.2 months median follow-up, ORR 86.1% at RP2D and 100% in BCMA/GPRC5D-naive patients, CRS 59% with ZERO events grade 3 or higher, and a schedule of ONE 5 mg step-up then 100 mg MONTHLY - in a class where approved bispecifics need weekly dosing and multiple step-ups. WHAT THE AVIDITY GATE DID NOT FIX, and structurally cannot: grade 3+ infections 28%, taste disturbance 58%, 4 treatment-related deaths. Both toxicities are on-target on normal tissue - BCMA on normal plasma cells (hypogammaglobulinemia, then infection) and GPRC5D on hard keratinized tissue (the taste/nail problem this show covered with talquetamab on 2026-06-15). A two-antigen avidity gate spares tissue carrying ONE antigen; normal plasma cells carry BOTH. THE LANE IS CROWDED AND ALREADY CLINICAL: besides JNJ-5322 (FDA fast track), Innovent's IBI3003 (GPRC5D x BCMA x CD3) is in Phase 1/2 in China and Australia with US plans, and MBS314 (GPRC5D x BCMA x CD3) has reported updated dose-escalation results. GSK doses its first patient in 2027. "Potential best-in-class" means something different when the class leader has 126 patients and a monthly schedule and you have a mouse. WHY THE NON-DISCLOSURE IS THE MOST INFORMATIVE LINE IN THE RELEASE: "validated" narrows the myeloma options to roughly BCMA, GPRC5D, FcRH5 and CD38. Two readings - either the pair is the obvious one and GSK would rather not invite the side-by-side with a competitor three years ahead, or the pair is genuinely unusual (something with FcRH5 in it, cf. cevostamab covered 2026-07-24) and they are protecting it. The episode leans weakly toward the second. THE ARGUMENT GSK SHOULD HAVE LED WITH: antigen escape. Biallelic BCMA loss after BCMA-directed therapy and GPRC5D loss/mutation after GPRC5D-directed therapy are both documented; a dual-antigen engager covers escape from either. That is the durability claim, it has published support, and it is the one still open - tolerability has already been answered by someone else. GSK'S OWN SEQUENCING PROBLEM: its existing myeloma franchise is belantamab mafodotin, a BCMA-directed ADC. If the trispecific includes BCMA, GSK will be selling two BCMA-directed agents into overlapping patients, and whether ADC exposure selects the antigen-loss clones that later blunt the engager becomes an internal question. THE DESIGN POINT: what GSK actually paid for is not the third specificity, it is the attenuated CD3 arm and the valency that makes attenuation survivable. Eleven days ago this show covered AbbVie's etentamig (ABBV-383) - a plain BISPECIFIC, one tumor antigen, with a deliberately weak (~1.3 uM) CD3 arm and bivalent high-avidity BCMA binding - which posted 28.3% CRS with ZERO grade 3+ in Phase 3. Same grammar, one fewer antigen, same safety result. Avidity-gated CD3 is what buys the clean cytokine table; the second tumor antigen has to earn its keep on escape and depth of response. WATCH IN 2027: not the safety table, which will probably look fine, but whether anything in the data says this molecule needed to be a trispecific at all.
item.itunes:summary: GSK announced this morning that it is acquiring a preclinical trispecific T cell engager for multiple myeloma from Chimagen Biosciences - full global rights, undisclosed upfront, up to $750 million in total value, Phase 1 in 2027 - and it will not say what the two tumor antigens are. That non-disclosure is the most informative line in the release, and the episode builds around it. First the money: this is GSK's second Chimagen purchase, and the 2024 one (CMG1A46, a CD19 x CD20 x CD3 engager) carried $300 million up front and a larger headline total, for a molecule already in the clinic. A smaller total and an undisclosed upfront for a preclinical asset says GSK is buying a second copy of a platform rather than a specific drug. That platform, TRIAD, is worth knowing: an IgG-like ~151 kDa molecule in 1:(1+1) valency, a single deliberately low-affinity CD3 arm against one high-affinity arm each for two tumor antigens, so selectivity comes from avidity rather than affinity. The CMG1A46 preclinical data quantify what that buys - 0.3 pM lysis EC50, cynomolgus tolerance at six times the dose of a conventional CD3 x CD20 bispecific, CD3 occupancy settling at 20-30% instead of saturating, cytokines peaking at 4-8 hours and back to baseline by 24. Where the episode disagrees is with GSK's stated rationale. The release leads on the class's difficult tolerability, but the leading trispecific in this exact space already answered that: Johnson and Johnson's JNJ-5322 reported 86% responses at the recommended dose, 100% in target-naive patients, cytokine release syndrome in 59% with not one event at grade 3 or above, and monthly dosing after a single step-up. What it did not fix is what an avidity gate structurally cannot fix - 28% grade 3+ infections and 58% taste disturbance, both on-target on normal tissue that carries both antigens. Meanwhile the BCMA x GPRC5D x CD3 lane already has Innovent's IBI3003 and MBS314 in the clinic alongside JNJ-5322, and GSK doses its first patient in 2027. "Potential best-in-class" reads differently when the leader has 126 patients and you have a mouse. Unless the targets are not the obvious pair - which is the reading the episode leans toward, weakly. The argument GSK should have led with is antigen escape, where documented biallelic BCMA loss and GPRC5D mutation give the dual-antigen design a durability rationale that is still genuinely open. And the design point for anyone building these: what GSK paid for is the attenuated CD3 arm, not the third specificity. AbbVie's etentamig - a plain bispecific with a deliberately weak CD3 arm - posted 28.3% CRS with zero grade 3+ in Phase 3 eleven days ago on this show. Same grammar, one fewer antigen, same safety result.
